title: Former Lions Graham Glasgow Joins Multiple Ex-Players in Tuesday Tryout Showcase – Pride of Detroit
body:
Detroit’s former players were among the most prominent names on the NFL’s Tuesday transaction list, as several ex‑Lions earned tryout invitations from teams looking to add depth on the offensive line and at other positions. The most notable of those invited was veteran guard Graham Glasgow, who received a tryout from the Baltimore Ravens alongside former Lions center Jarron Cox. In total, at least six former Detroit players appeared on the day’s tryout roster, underscoring the Lions’ recent history of producing serviceable, if not star‑level, talent that remains attractive to clubs seeking low‑cost, experienced options.

The Ravens’ decision to evaluate Glasgow and Cox reflects a broader trend in the league: teams are increasingly turning to free‑agent tryouts as a way to fill roster spots without committing to long‑term contracts. Both Glasgow and Cox spent the better part of the past three seasons in Detroit’s offensive line rotation, with Glasgow starting 32 games at guard and Cox serving as a reliable backup center. Their familiarity with a pro‑style offense and ability to step in on short notice make them ideal candidates for a team like Baltimore, which has struggled with interior line consistency following injuries to key starters earlier this season.

Other former Lions who attracted interest on Tuesday included defensive end Kony Edewor‑Bam, who was invited to a tryout with the New York Giants, and wide receiver James Starks, who received a look from the New England Patriots. Edewor‑Bam, a former second‑round pick, posted 7.5 sacks last season with Detroit and could provide the Giants with a versatile edge‑rusher capable of rotating in on passing downs. Starks, a former Pro Bowl receiver who spent the last two years on the Lions’ practice squad, is looking to revive a career that once featured three 1,000‑yard seasons. The Patriots, known for extracting value from veteran talent, may see Starks as a low‑risk addition to a receiving corps that has been plagued by injuries.

Analysts note that the concentration of former Lions on the transaction list is partially a byproduct of Detroit’s recent roster turnover. Since the 2022 season, the Lions have undergone a near‑complete overhaul of their coaching staff and front office, resulting in a surplus of players who were released or not re‑signed as the franchise re‑tools. This churn has created a pool of experienced professionals who are now free agents, and other teams are capitalizing on the opportunity to evaluate them without the financial commitment of a guaranteed contract.

From a strategic standpoint, the tryout model benefits both parties. Players like Glasgow and Cox receive a platform to showcase their health and skill level, potentially earning a spot on a 53‑man roster or practice squad. Meanwhile, clubs can conduct hands‑on assessments that go beyond film study, testing players’ current conditioning, scheme fit, and locker‑room chemistry. The NFL’s collective bargaining agreement permits teams to hold up to 12 tryouts per week, and the recent surge in such invitations suggests that franchises are leaning heavily on this mechanism as the season progresses and injuries mount.

Looking ahead, the outcomes of these tryouts could have ripple effects for the Lions’ own roster decisions. If former Detroit players secure new contracts elsewhere, it may reinforce the perception that the organization’s recent drafting and development strategies have produced quality depth. Conversely, if the tryouts yield few signings, Detroit could face criticism for not retaining or adequately developing its own talent. For the players themselves, the next few weeks will be decisive; a successful audition could extend their NFL careers, while a missed opportunity may signal the end of their time in the league. In any case, Tuesday’s transaction list highlights how former Lions continue to be a valuable resource across the NFL, and how the tryout system remains a crucial avenue for veteran players seeking to stay in the game.
